questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a website on the Internet?

options.A: To serve as a physical storage of files.
options.B: To provide an interactive interface for users to access information and services.
options.C: To connect multiple computers in a local network.
options.D: To function only as a business platform.

questions.explanation: A website acts as a digital interface that allows users to interact with content, services, and information hosted on the web.

questions.question_text: When you access a website, how does your computer communicate with the server?

options.A: By sending a phone signal to the server.
options.B: By transmitting packets of data over the Internet using standardized protocols.
options.C: By directly connecting to the website’s database.
options.D: By using only your browser's cache memory.

questions.explanation: Computers communicate over the internet by breaking down information into data packets and sending them using protocols like HTTP/HTTPS.

questions.question_text: What role does DNS (Domain Name System) play on the Internet?

options.A: It stores website files on the server.
options.B: It translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
options.C: It manages user requests for website data.
options.D: It provides security for websites through encryption.

questions.explanation: DNS acts like a phonebook for the internet, converting names like 'google.com' into numerical IP addresses that computers understand.

questions.question_text: Which of the following combinations best describes the role of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a webpage?

options.A: HTML for structure, CSS for style, JavaScript for interactivity.
options.B: HTML for style, CSS for structure, JavaScript for security.
options.C: HTML for databases, CSS for animations, JavaScript for content.
options.D: HTML for hosting, CSS for DNS, JavaScript for coding.

questions.explanation: HTML defines the content and structure, CSS handles the visual presentation and layout, and JavaScript adds dynamic behavior and interactivity.

questions.question_text: What happens during an HTTP request?

options.A: The browser asks the server for data, and the server sends back the requested data.
options.B: The browser downloads all files from the server.
options.C: The server creates a new copy of the website for every request.
options.D: The server sends requests to other browsers for backup.

questions.explanation: HTTP is a request-response protocol where a client (browser) requests resources and the server provides the appropriate response.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key difference between frontend and backend development?

options.A: Frontend focuses on server-side operations, while backend focuses on user interface.
options.B: Frontend involves creating the user interface, while backend handles server-side logic and databases.
options.C: Frontend developers manage hosting, while backend developers manage DNS.
options.D: Frontend and backend are the same and used interchangeably.

questions.explanation: Frontend refers to what the user sees and interacts with, whereas backend refers to the server, application, and database logic working behind the scenes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major impact of the Internet on businesses since the 1990s?

options.A: Reduced reliance on technology for customer interactions.
options.B: Increased barriers to entry for small businesses.
options.C: Global reach and accessibility through e-commerce platforms.
options.D: Decline in consumer engagement and communication.

questions.explanation: The internet revolutionized business by allowing even small companies to reach a global audience through digital storefronts and online marketing.

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason for defining business objectives before building a website?

options.A: To choose the right color scheme
options.B: To ensure the website aligns with the business’s goals and user needser
options.C: To make the website load faster
options.D: To design a more visually appealing homepage

questions.explanation: Defining objectives ensures that the design and functionality of the site serve a purpose, such as lead generation or sales, while meeting user expectations.

questions.question_text: Which factor should guide feature prioritization when building a website?
questions.explanation: Features should be prioritized based on how effectively they fulfill the core goals of the business and provide value to the target audience.

questions.question_text: Which color is most commonly associated with trust and reliability in website design?
questions.explanation: In color theory, blue is frequently used by corporate, financial, and tech brands because it evokes feelings of stability, trust, and professionalism.

questions.question_text: Which typography factor most affects a website’s readability?
questions.explanation: Adequate font size and line spacing (leading) are critical for ensuring that users can easily consume text content without eye strain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following makes a Call to Action (CTA) more effective?

options.B: Making the CTA button blend into the website design
options.C: Using clear, action-oriented language like "Get Started" or "Join Now"
options.D: Placing the CTA at the very bottom, hidden from immediate view

questions.explanation: Effective CTAs use persuasive, verb-driven language and high-contrast design to guide users toward a specific conversion goal.

questions.question_text: Which principle is most important for a good user interface (UI)?

options.A: Using complex animations to impress users
options.C: Filling the page with as much content as possible
options.D: Using only bright colors to capture attention

questions.explanation: A good UI focuses on making the user experience seamless, reducing cognitive load through simple, clean layouts and easy-to-follow navigation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key difference between web and desktop design?

options.A: Desktop websites load faster than web versions
options.B: Web design must prioritize responsiveness for different screen sizes
options.C: Desktop interfaces are always more user-friendly than web interfaces
options.D: Web design doesn’t need navigation menus

questions.explanation: Unlike desktop-only software, web design must be responsive to ensure it looks and functions well across mobiles, tablets, and various desktop resolutions.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of HTML in web development?
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) provides the backbone of a webpage by organizing text, images, and other elements into a logical structure.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the header tag in HTML?

options.A: To define the main content of the page
options.C: To group introductory content like titles and navigation
options.D: To store metadata like CSS and JavaScript

questions.explanation: The `<header>` element is a semantic tag used to contain introductory items, logos, and navigation links for a page or section.

questions.question_text: Which of the following elements contains the visible content of a webpage?
questions.explanation: While the `<head>` contains metadata, the `<body>` tag contains all the visual elements like text, images, and buttons that users see.

questions.question_text: Why is indentation important in code?

options.A: It affects how styles are applied
options.B: It improves code readability and organization
options.D: It is required for CSS to work properly

questions.explanation: Proper indentation makes code easier for humans to read and maintain by clearly showing the hierarchy and relationship between nested elements.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the paragraph tag in HTML?

options.B: To insert a paragraph of text

questions.explanation:
The `

` tag is used to define blocks of text, automatically adding space before and after the block for better readability.

questions.question_text: All HTML elements must have both an opening and a closing tag.
questions.explanation:
Some elements, known as void or self-closing elements (like ``, `
`, and ``), do not require a closing tag.

questions.question_text: An unordered list unordered list automatically numbers the list items.
questions.explanation: Unordered lists (`<ul>`) use bullet points. Numbered lists are created using the ordered list (`<ol>`) tag.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the href attribute in an anchor tag?

options.A: It defines the text color of the link
options.B: It specifies the URL or destination of the link
options.C: It adds an image inside the link

questions.explanation: The `href` attribute (Hypertext Reference) tells the browser exactly where to take the user when the link is clicked.

questions.question_text: Which attribute is required in the img tag to specify the image file location?
questions.explanation: The `src` (source) attribute points to the file path or URL of the image to be displayed on the page.

questions.question_text: Which syntax is used to write a comment in HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML comments are written using the `<!-- comment text -->` syntax and are not displayed by the browser.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of an inline element in HTML?
questions.explanation: Inline elements like `<span>` only take up as much width as necessary and do not start on a new line, unlike block elements.

questions.question_text: Which HTML element is used to define an input field in a form?
questions.explanation: The `<input>` tag is the primary element used to collect user data, with various types like text, password, and checkbox.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the button tag in HTML?

options.B: To submit a form or trigger an action

questions.explanation: The `<button>` element is used to perform actions like submitting a form or executing a JavaScript function when clicked.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the name attribute in an HTML form element?

options.A: To define the style of the element
options.B: To provide an identifier for form data when submitted
options.C: To make the element required in the form
options.D: To specify the destination URL of the form

questions.explanation: The `name` attribute acts as a key for the data value being sent to the server, allowing the backend to identify which input corresponds to which piece of data.

questions.question_text: Which of the following HTML elements is used to define a table row?
questions.explanation: The `<tr>` tag stands for 'table row' and is used to group table cells (`<td>` or `<th>`) horizontally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a semantic HTML element?
questions.explanation: Semantic tags like `<article>` describe the meaning of the content to the browser and search engines, whereas `<div>` is purely generic.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of CSS?

options.A: To add interactivity to a webpage
options.B: To define the structure of a webpage
options.C: To style and format HTML elements
options.D: To store and manage website data

questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is used to control the layout, colors, fonts, and overall visual appearance of HTML elements.

questions.question_text: Which method is the most efficient for applying styles across multiple web pages?
questions.explanation: External CSS uses a separate .css file linked to multiple HTML pages, allowing for centralized style management and faster load times via caching.

questions.question_text: Which CSS selector is used to target an element with a specific ID?
questions.explanation: The `#` symbol is used in CSS to target elements by their unique `id` attribute.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a valid way to define a color in CSS?
questions.explanation: CSS supports multiple formats for colors, including named colors, Hexadecimal codes, and RGB/RGBA functional notation.

questions.question_text: Which CSS property is used to change the font type of text?
questions.explanation: The `font-family` property allows you to specify a prioritized list of fonts for the browser to use for the selected element.

questions.question_text: Which browser tool is commonly used to inspect and modify CSS in real time?
questions.explanation: The 'Inspect Element' tool (part of Browser Developer Tools) allows developers to see and temporarily change CSS to debug layouts live.

questions.question_text: Which part of the CSS Box Model defines the space outside an element’s border?
questions.explanation: Margin creates transparent space around the outside of an element's border, separating it from adjacent elements.

questions.question_text: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: Inline styles take precedence over external or internal stylesheets because they have the highest specificity rating (1,0,0,0).

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors affect CSS specificity? (Select all that apply)

options.A: The order in which styles are written
options.B: The type of selector used (ID, class, element)
options.C: The number of times a rule is repeated
options.D: Whether styles are applied inside an HTML attribute

questions.explanation: Specificity is calculated based on selector types (ID > Class > Element) and where the style is declared (Inline is highest). Order only matters if specificity is equal.

questions.question_text: Which combinator selects only the direct children of an element?
questions.explanation: The child combinator (`>`) targets only elements that are immediate children of the parent, ignoring deeper descendants.

questions.question_text: Which pseudo-class applies styles when a user hovers over an element?
questions.explanation: The `:hover` pseudo-class allows developers to change an element's style when the user's mouse pointer enters its area.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the span tag in HTML?

options.A: To define a new block-level section
options.B: To group inline elements for styling

questions.explanation: The `<span>` tag is a generic inline container used to hook specific parts of text or other inline elements for targeted CSS styling.

questions.question_text: Which display value makes an element behave like a block element but allows it to stay inline with other elements?
questions.explanation: `inline-block` allows an element to have width/height like a block element while remaining flowable on the same line as other content.

questions.question_text: An element with position: absolute; is always positioned relative to the body element.
questions.explanation: An absolutely positioned element is relative to its nearest *positioned* ancestor. If none exist, it defaults to the body.

questions.question_text: Using clear: both; ensures that an element will not be positioned next to floated elements on either side.
questions.explanation: The `clear` property specifies that floating elements are not allowed to float beside the element, forcing it to move below them.

questions.question_text: In JavaScript, a class can contain both constructor methods and custom methods.
questions.explanation: Classes serve as templates for objects, utilizing a constructor to initialize properties and custom methods to define behaviors.

questions.question_text: Why are CSS layout techniques important in web development?

options.A: They help define the structure and positioning of elements on a webpage
options.B: They are only used for adding color and fonts to text
options.C: They slow down the website loading time
options.D: They are used to write server-side scripts

questions.explanation: Layout techniques like Flexbox and Grid allow developers to create organized, responsive, and complex structures that adapt to different screens.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of using Flexbox in CSS?

options.B: To simplify the alignment and distribution of space within a container
options.C: To change the background color of a web page
options.D: To define custom fonts and text styles

questions.explanation: Flexbox (Flexible Box Layout) is designed for one-dimensional layouts, making it easy to align items in a row or column and distribute space dynamically.

questions.question_text: What makes CSS Grid different from Flexbox?

options.A: Grid is only used for adding color to the page
options.B: Grid allows you to create two-dimensional layouts (rows and columns)
options.C: Grid is used to animate text
options.D: Grid is a JavaScript feature, not CSS

questions.explanation: While Flexbox is primarily for 1D layouts (row OR column), CSS Grid is for 2D layouts, allowing simultaneous control of both rows and columns.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of media queries in CSS?

options.C: To apply CSS styles based on device characteristics

questions.explanation: Media queries are the cornerstone of responsive design, allowing styles to change based on screen width, resolution, or device orientation.

questions.question_text: What is Bootstrap mainly used for in web development?
questions.explanation: Bootstrap is a popular CSS framework that provides pre-styled components and a grid system to speed up the development of responsive websites.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about JavaScript are true?

options.A: JavaScript is a server-side programming language only.
options.B: JavaScript can manipulate HTML and CSS to create dynamic web pages.
options.D: JavaScript code can only be written inside an external .js file.

questions.explanation: JavaScript is primarily used for client-side interactivity and follows strict casing rules. It can also be written inline or within `<script>` tags.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are true about JavaScript development in the browser?

options.A: The alert() function is used to display messages in the browser as a popup.
options.B: The Chrome Console allows you to write and test JavaScript code in real-time.
options.C: JavaScript does not require a specific syntax and can be written freely.
options.D: Chrome Developer Tools are useful for debugging JavaScript code.

questions.explanation: Browsers provide the console and developer tools for testing and debugging, while functions like `alert()` provide simple user feedback.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primitive data type in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Primitives are the most basic data types (String, Number, Boolean, Null, Undefined, Symbol, BigInt). Objects and Arrays are reference types.

questions.question_text: Which keyword is used to declare a block-scoped variable in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: `let` and `const` were introduced in ES6 to provide block scoping, whereas `var` is function-scoped.

questions.question_text: What does the prompt() function do in JavaScript?

options.A: Displays a message and waits for user input
options.B: Logs data to the browser console
options.D: Shows a confirmation dialog with OK and Cancel

questions.explanation: The `prompt()` method displays a dialog box with an optional message prompting the user to input some text.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a valid JavaScript variable name that follows camelCase convention?
questions.explanation: Camel case starts with a lowercase letter and capitalizes the first letter of each subsequent word without spaces or underscores.

questions.question_text: Which of the following variable declarations allows reassignment of its value?
questions.explanation: Variables declared with `let` and `var` can be reassigned, while `const` creates a read-only reference that cannot be changed.
The `+` operator concatenates the strings together, including the space character assigned between the two variables.
The `toUpperCase()` method returns the calling string value converted to all uppercase characters.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly uses a template literal to print "Hello, Alice!"?
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks (`) and the `${}` syntax to embed expressions and variables directly into a string.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about null and undefined in JavaScript?

options.A: undefined is the default value of a declared but uninitialized variable.
options.B: null means the variable has not been declared.
options.C: Both null and undefined are the same in JavaScript.
options.D: null is automatically assigned by JavaScript when a variable is declared.

questions.explanation: `undefined` is what JavaScript gives a variable that exists but has no value. `null` is an intentional assignment representing 'nothing'.
The remainder operator (`%`) returns the remainder left over after division (10 divided by 3 is 3 with a remainder of 1).

questions.question_text: What does the Math.floor(4.9) return in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: `Math.floor()` rounds a number down to the nearest integer, regardless of the decimal value.
Since 85 is not greater than 90 but is greater than 70, the second condition is met and 'Good' is printed.
The outer condition (20 >= 18) is true, and the nested inner condition (hasID is true) is also true, resulting in 'Entry allowed'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following values is considered falsy in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, falsy values include `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN`. Empty arrays and objects are truthy.

questions.question_text:
How do you access the second element in the following array?
let fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"];
questions.explanation: JavaScript arrays use zero-based indexing, so the first element is at index 0 and the second element is at index 1.
`push()` adds 'blue' to the end, then `shift()` removes 'red' from the beginning, leaving ['green', 'blue'].
The `slice(start, end)` method returns elements from index 'start' up to, but not including, 'end'. Index 1 and 2 are Mumbai and Bangalore.
The `map()` method creates a new array by applying the provided function to every element in the original array.
Object properties can be accessed using dot notation (`object.property`) or bracket notation (`object['property']`).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about JavaScript loops are true?

options.A: A while loop may never run if the condition is false at the beginning.
options.B: A do...while loop always runs at least once.
options.C: You can use break to exit a loop early.
options.D: A for loop cannot be used to iterate over an array.

questions.explanation: While loops check the condition first; do...while checks it after the first run. `for` loops are the standard way to iterate over arrays.
The function takes the string 'Alex' as an argument and returns a concatenated greeting including that string.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the Document Object Model (DOM)?

options.A: A JavaScript framework used to build web apps
options.B: A programming language used to style HTML pages
options.C: An interface that allows programs to manipulate HTML and XML documents
options.D: A type of server that hosts websites

questions.explanation: The DOM is a tree-like representation of the webpage that JavaScript can use to change content, structure, and styles dynamically.

questions.question_text: Where in an HTML document is it generally recommended to place the script tag for better page load performance?

options.B: At the beginning of the body section
options.C: At the end of the body section

questions.explanation: Placing scripts before the closing `</body>` tag ensures the HTML structure is loaded and visible before the browser starts executing heavy JavaScript.

questions.question_text: The querySelectorAll() method returns a single element from the DOM.
questions.explanation: `querySelectorAll()` returns a static NodeList containing all elements that match the specified CSS selector, unlike `querySelector()` which returns only the first.

questions.question_text: Which property would you use to access the next sibling element of a selected DOM node?
questions.explanation: `nextElementSibling` returns the element immediately following the specified one in the same tree level.

questions.question_text: The method element.remove() permanently deletes the element from the DOM.
questions.explanation: The `remove()` method removes the element from the Document Object Model tree, though it may still exist in memory if referenced by a variable.

questions.question_text: You can add multiple event listeners of the same type to a single DOM element.
questions.explanation: Using `addEventListener()` allows you to attach multiple different functions to the same event (e.g., two different 'click' handlers) on one element.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about WordPress is true?

options.A: WordPress requires advanced coding knowledge to build a website
options.B: You cannot use plugins in WordPress
options.C: WordPress allows you to create and manage websites without writing code
options.D: WordPress is only used for blogging

questions.explanation: WordPress is a Content Management System (CMS) designed to allow users to build complex websites using a visual interface and pre-built themes/plugins.

questions.question_text: You must know how to code in HTML and CSS to build a website on WordPress.
questions.explanation: While coding knowledge helps for advanced customization, WordPress provides drag-and-drop tools and themes that make it possible to build sites without coding.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential use of ChatGPT in a WordPress-based website?

options.A: Generating lorem ipsum placeholder text only
options.C: Hosting and managing your website's server

questions.explanation: AI models like ChatGPT are commonly used to assist in content creation, providing drafts for posts, FAQs, and marketing copy for websites.
